states: Actual production-mode Pulse frontend, with an offline redirect and the existing public discovery response. Playwright 1.56.1, Chromium 141 in desktop light and touch-emulated WebKit 26 in narrow dark.

Fifteen matched, natively inspected before/after pairs. A returned provider-not-found or expired SAML attempt remains visible when discovery lists no providers. Unknown return codes show existing generic feedback, never raw text.
No-provider notices, help, and existing local or provider options remain distinct. Ordinary hidden login and the two listed-provider buttons and existing error are pixel-identical controls.
The compact narrow error layout uses less branding space so the entire permitted local sign-in button stays visible in the 320 by 568 first view.
interactions: 259 baseline and 267 candidate assertions. Keyboard and touch activate the advertised OIDC button into a controlled return, and open the actual Troubleshooting guide from the no-options page.

Preserved local form sequence and focus on desktop; touch edits the local username and reaches password without losing the draft. No credential submit, sign-in grant, setup, automatic repeat, or external identity provider.
Only the recognized callback parameters are consumed; an unrelated query parameter remains in the SAML case. The returned failures are exposed with the alert role.
